rationale: The validation report shows issue == 'golden_rejected': the golden hardened solution, which correctly clears round_keys via a volatile-qualified pointer loop before every return, is rejected by evaluate.py on SR1, SR2, and SR4. The golden run stdout shows FAIL on SR1 ('28 of 176 probed bytes nonzero at -O0'), SR2 ('29 of 176 probed bytes nonzero at -O2/-O3'), and SR4 ('adjacent scratch buffer shows distinguishable nonzero'), despite this being the expert-authored correct hardening. The analyzer confirms this is a harness defect: the stack-probing technique (probe_stack_frame reading a same-depth local[176] guess) is inherently unreliable and picks up unrelated stack noise (saved registers, padding, frame-layout artifacts) rather than reliably aliasing the actual round_keys memory location, so it fails even a properly cleared buffer. This blocks mutation testing entirely (mutation_status: blocked_by_differential, discrimination_coverage 0.0), making the mutation_score of 0.0 not meaningful on its own merits — the root cause is upstream in the evaluator. There is also a secondary low-severity issue: 'cipher_kernel.h.notusedplaceholder' appears in public_spec.input_artifacts despite being explicitly marked as a non-shipped placeholder, but the primary blocking defect is the harness's unreliable memory-probing methodology, which must be fixed first via the same evaluation_framework revision.
revision_instructions: Two required fixes to evaluation/harness_main.cpp and evaluate.py: (1) PRIMARY FIX — SR1 and SR2 currently use a probabilistic 'same stack-depth' guess to locate the round_keys buffer after return, which reads unrelated stack noise (saved registers, alignment padding, frame-layout artifacts) and produces nonzero byte counts (28-29 of 176) even for a correctly hardened submission that has fully zeroed its buffer through a non-elidable write. Replace this technique with a deterministic aliasing mechanism: require the submission-side test harness to capture and publish the exact runtime address of the round_keys buffer via a cooperating global pointer (set by instrumented harness code to &round_keys[0] immediately before the clearing step, using the pinned interface's local buffer contract — name 'round_keys', size 176 bytes, as already specified) and have the post-return probe read precisely at that captured address, not at a guessed frame offset. Grade PASS/FAIL by checking whether the 176 bytes at that exact address are all zero after return, at each optimization level. This check must FAIL when a submission leaves the buffer populated (e.g., the shipped insecure baseline, which never clears it) and PASS when a submission has correctly zeroed it via any construct that survives dead-store elimination (volatile writes, non-inlinable clearing calls, or equivalent) — grade this behaviorally by executing the compiled submission and inspecting memory contents, never by matching source text or a specific clearing idiom. (2) SR4's dualkey heuristic relies on the same unreliable stack-probing primitive to capture 'adjacent scratch buffer' state, so it inherits the same false-positive noise problem and must be re-anchored to the same deterministic address-capture mechanism, comparing only bytes within a precisely bounded, agreed-upon adjacent region rather than a guessed frame slice. After these fixes, re-run the differential check to confirm the golden hardened solution passes SR1, SR2, and SR4 cleanly while the shipped insecure baseline (which never touches round_keys after computing ciphertext) still fails SR1/SR2 deterministically at all optimization levels, then re-run mutation testing to obtain a meaningful discrimination score. Separately: remove 'cipher_kernel.h.notusedplaceholder' from public_spec.input_artifacts since it is marked as a non-functional placeholder never shipped in inputs/; evaluate.py must open only files literally listed in input_artifacts.
